cards.front: [___] refers to the clinician's emotional reactions to a patient that may compromise care if unrecognised.
cards.context: Regular supervision is the primary safeguard.

cards.front: Complex PTSD (ICD-11) adds Disturbances in Self-Organisation to PTSD core symptoms: affect dysregulation, [___], and disturbed relationships.
cards.context: Complex PTSD arises from prolonged, repeated trauma (childhood abuse, domestic violence, captivity) where escape is difficult, as opposed to single-incident trauma.

cards.front: In a young woman with new-onset psychosis, seizures, and dyskinesias, the priority diagnosis to exclude is [___] encephalitis.
cards.context:
Always exclude organic psychosis before diagnosing a primary psychiatric disorder.

Anti-NMDA encephalitis presents in young women with the triad: psychosis + seizures + orofacial dyskinesias. ~50% have an ovarian teratoma — screen for it.

cards.front: In the FRAMES brief intervention model, the [___] component offers patients a range of change strategies rather than a single directive.
cards.context: FRAMES (Feedback, Responsibility, Advice, Menu of options, Empathy, Self-efficacy) structures brief alcohol interventions in primary care.

cards.front: Combination NRT pairs a nicotine [___] for background replacement with a short-acting form (gum, lozenge, or inhaler) for breakthrough cravings.
cards.context: The patch provides steady-state nicotine replacement to prevent baseline withdrawal, while short-acting forms manage situational breakthrough cravings.
